16:30 local, 15:30 GMT, 21:00 IST: Four of England’s first seven wickets fell to spin - not something you would associate too often with ODI cricket in England. But this has been that kind of day. Opting to bat, England lost Banton early, but Duckett and Root settled in nicely, respecting the good balls and putting the bad ones away. They added 39 in the final four overs of the mandatory powerplay, but the introduction of spin changed the complexion of the innings. Duckett was trapped lbw by Wellalage, with the surface offering enough grip and variable bounce to make batting increasingly tricky.

Root and Brook then steadied things with a 68-run stand, and it looked like one of the Yorkshire pair might go on to make a hundred. Not to be. Root was undone by a beauty from debutant Colombage for 44, while Brook fell trying to up the ante soon after bringing up his 7th ODI fifty. England slipped from 182/3 to 211/7 and looked in danger of being bowled out for under 250. But Atkinson’s sensible resistance, coupled with some useful boundaries from Will Jacks, helped them scrape their way to a competitive total. There are enough tricks in this surface, and the hosts will fancy their chances of making Sri Lanka work hard for their runs. Let’s see how the chase unfolds. Back in 30.
